items.title: 1.1.3 Complex Numbers as Ordered Pairs of Real Numbers

source_refs.note: 1.1.3 ordered-pair definition, properties (i)-(iv) and Example 1 (book p. 2); PDF 7-7.

blocks.text: 1.1.3 Complex Numbers as Ordered Pairs of Real Numbers
We can also define complex numbers by using ordered pairs. Let \(C\) be the set of ordered pairs belonging to \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}\) which are subject to the following properties:

items: \((a, b) = (c, d) \Leftrightarrow a = c \wedge b = d\)

blocks.text: Then \(C\) is called the set of complex numbers. It is easy to see that \[(a, b) - (c, d) = (a - c,\ b - d)\]

items: If \(k\) is any real number, then \(k(a, b) = (ka, kb)\).

blocks.text: Properties (i), (ii) and (iii) respectively define equality, sum and difference of two complex numbers. Property (iv) defines the product of a real number and a complex number.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints that (i), (ii) and (iii) define "equality, sum and difference". Property (iii) \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd,\ ad+bc)\) defines the product of two complex numbers; the difference is the result \((a,b)-(c,d) = (a-c,\ b-d)\) stated after it.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
The pair \((a, b)\) is just another way of writing \(a + ib\): first component = real part, second component = imaginary part. For example \((8, 9)\) means \(8 + 9i\) and \((5, -6)\) means \(5 - 6i\).
The product rule (iii) is exactly the multiplication rule of 1.1.2: \((a+ib)(c+id) = (ac-bd) + i(ad+bc)\).
In this language \(i = (0, 1)\). Using (iii):
\[(0,1)(0,1) = (0\cdot0 - 1\cdot1,\ 0\cdot1 + 1\cdot0)\]
\[= (-1,\ 0)\]
and \((-1, 0)\) is the real number \(-1\). So the ordered-pair definition gives \(i^2 = -1\) without "inventing" \(\sqrt{-1}\).

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: Find the sum, difference and product of the complex numbers \((8, 9)\) and \((5, -6)\).
steps:
Given: \(z_1 = (8, 9)\) and \(z_2 = (5, -6)\).
To find: \(z_1 + z_2\), \(z_1 - z_2\) and \(z_1 z_2\).
Method: use the ordered-pair rules: (ii) for the sum, \((a,b)-(c,d) = (a-c, b-d)\) for the difference, and (iii) \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd, ad+bc)\) for the product, with \(a = 8, b = 9, c = 5, d = -6\).

Step 1: the sum
\[(8, 9) + (5, -6)\]
\[= (8+5,\ 9+(-6))\]
\[= (13,\ 3)\]
Why: rule (ii) adds the first components together and the second components together.

Step 2: the difference
The book prints: \((8-5,\ 9-(-6)) = (5,\ 15)\)
Working it out:
\[(8, 9) - (5, -6)\]
\[= (8-5,\ 9-(-6))\]
\[= (3,\ 9+6)\]
\[= (3,\ 15)\]
Why: subtract component by component; subtracting \(-6\) is the same as adding \(6\), and \(8 - 5 = 3\).

Step 3: the product, first component \(ac - bd\)
\[8 \cdot 5 - (9)(-6)\]
\[= 40 + 54\]
\[= 94\]
Why: in \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd,\ ad+bc)\) the first component is \(ac - bd\); here \(bd = 9 \times (-6) = -54\), so subtracting it adds 54.

Step 4: the product, second component \(ad + bc\)
\[8(-6) + 9 \cdot 5\]
\[= -48 + 45\]
\[= -3\]
Why: the second component is \(ad + bc\). The book writes it as \(9 \cdot 5 + (-6)(8)\), the same two products in the other order.
\[(8, 9)(5, -6) = (94,\ -3)\]

Check:
Write the numbers as \(8 + 9i\) and \(5 - 6i\) and multiply in the usual way:
\[(8+9i)(5-6i)\]
\[= 40 - 48i + 45i - 54i^2\]
\[= 40 + 54 - 3i\]
\[= 94 - 3i\]
This is \((94, -3)\). For the difference: \((3, 15) + (5, -6) = (8, 9)\), the first number again.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the difference as \((8-5,\ 9-(-6)) = (5,\ 15)\). Since \(8 - 5 = 3\), the correct difference is \((3, 15)\). The sum \((13, 3)\) and the product \((94, -3)\) are correct.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. \((a, b) \leftrightarrow a + ib\).
2. Equal pairs: both components equal.
3. Sum and difference: component by component.
4. Product: \((a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd,\ ad+bc)\); real multiple: \(k(a,b) = (ka, kb)\).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.text:
Multiplying component by component: \((a,b)(c,d) \ne (ac, bd)\). For example \((0,1)(0,1)\) is \((-1, 0)\), not \((0, 1)\).
Sign slips with negative components: \(9 - (-6) = 15\), and \(-(9)(-6) = +54\).
